summary:
Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug stands under the national framework of the Russian Federation. The federal statutes governing gender identity and sexual orientation apply within the okrug unaltered, and no regional deviation from the national position has been identified, so the national assessment governs what a visitor faces here.

Same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised in Russia, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are both banned. Gender-marker changes on official documents are prohibited and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, so a visitor's papers cannot be brought into line with their presentation: any police, hotel or transport identity check reads a mismatch that no supporting document can resolve, and no lawful route to obtain gender-affirming care exists during a stay.

The 2013 "gay propaganda" statute is punishable by administrative fines of up to 400,000 rubles for individuals or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences escalating to criminal prosecution and up to four years' imprisonment. Foreigners who breach these provisions face arrest, short detention and deportation, and the expanded law reaches public expression that justifies gender transition.

Since the November 2023 Supreme Court designation of the international LGBT+ movement as extremist, participation carries two to six years' imprisonment and organising carries six to ten years under Article 282.2. Human Rights Watch recorded 101 extremism-related convictions arising from that designation as of 30 June 2025, of which about 98 were administrative and three criminal.

The volume of extremism cases is now substantial. Between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges connected to the designation, including three publishing-house staff charged in May 2025 under Article 282.2 who each face up to 12 years' imprisonment. A further 81 people were found guilty across 98 administrative cases under Article 20.3 for displaying banned symbols, meaning symbol display alone has produced convictions.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on Russia (SOGI, June 2025) records at least 139 people in Russia impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws between 2022 and 2024, and assesses that openly LGBT+ people are likely to face discriminatory treatment that, by its nature or repetition, may amount to persecution. Its assessment that the state is able but not willing to provide protection sets the standard applied to UK asylum claims, and it affirms that LGBT+ people constitute a particular social group under the refugee convention.
tangentialFactors:
The enforcement pattern is national rather than okrug-specific: convictions, raids and administrative cases are recorded across Russia since the 2023 designation, and nothing indicates that Yamalo-Nenets is insulated from federal policing priorities. A visitor should expect the same statutes to be applied by local officers as in any other region.

The composition of the caseload shows how broad the designation has become. Almost all of the 101 extremism convictions are administrative rather than criminal, and the separate Article 20.3 cases concern only the display of symbols, so exposure does not require attendance at any event or participation in any organisation.

Criminal exposure escalates with repetition and with role: single administrative offences draw fines or detention, while repeat propaganda offences become criminal, and organising within a designated extremist structure carries the longest sentence in the provisions cited. The three publishing-house staff charged in May 2025 face up to 12 years each, which indicates that employment and professional activity can attract the most serious charges.

The UK Home Office assessment sits alongside the federal provisions rather than altering them: it records the same bans on gender transition and gender-marker change, and adds an evidentiary record of at least 139 people affected between 2022 and 2024. That note is a finding about Russia as a whole, not a separate regime for the okrug.
localsOnly:
Residents of Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug live under the same federal position as the rest of Russia: same-sex sexual activity is lawful, but marriage for same-sex couples and gender transition are banned, gender-marker change on documents is unavailable, and trans-specific healthcare has been prohibited since 2023. There is no regional mechanism that alters any of these.

Local exposure follows the national penalty structure. Administrative offences under the propaganda statute attract fines up to 400,000 rubles or detention up to 15 days; repeat offences become criminal with up to four years; and Article 282.2 provides two to six years for participation and six to ten years for organising the designated extremist movement.

The UK Home Office note's conclusion that the state is able but not willing to protect openly LGBT+ people bears on residents who later claim asylum abroad, as does its finding that such people are likely to face discriminatory treatment amounting to persecution. It also affirms that LGBT+ people qualify as a particular social group under the refugee convention.

No okrug-level support provision, regional anti-discrimination body or local protection scheme for LGBT+ residents is recorded in the sources available for this entry.
outOfScopeNotes:
No okrug-specific enforcement data is available: the 101 extremism convictions, the 98 Article 20.3 administrative cases and the 139 people recorded by the UK Home Office are national totals, and the sources do not break them down by federal subject. Whether any of those cases arose within Yamalo-Nenets is unresolved.

No regional legislation, police directive or court decision specific to Yamalo-Nenets on gender identity or sexual orientation is sourced here. The absence of a recorded regional deviation is a research finding, not evidence that none exists in practice.

The sources do not address visitor entry screening, document inspection at airports within the okrug, availability of legal representation locally, or hate-crime sentencing enhancement in the region. Those points remain not sourced.
